meta.title: Board Metrics Builder
meta.note: A curated menu of board-ready security metrics with anchored guidance bands. Thresholds are seasoned-practitioner guidance, not compliance requirements; tune them to your program.

sources.name: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities and remediation guidance

metrics.name: Critical Asset EDR Coverage
metrics.question: What share of our most important systems can we actually see and defend in real time?
metrics.definition: The percentage of critical assets (servers, endpoints, and workloads deemed business-essential) running active endpoint detection and response agents that report to central monitoring.
metrics.boardFraming: Every unmonitored critical system is a blind spot where an attacker can operate unseen, raising the odds of a costly, undetected breach.

metrics.name: Mean Time to Respond, Critical
metrics.question: Once a serious incident starts, how quickly do we contain the damage?
metrics.definition: The average elapsed time, in hours, from detection of a critical incident to its containment or remediation across the reporting period.
metrics.boardFraming: The longer an attacker stays active, the more data, downtime, and recovery cost we absorb; faster containment directly limits financial loss.

metrics.name: Mean Time to Detect
metrics.question: How long do threats sit in our environment before we notice them?
metrics.definition: The average time, in days, between when an intrusion or malicious activity first begins and when our team detects it.
metrics.boardFraming: Threats that go undetected for days or weeks give attackers time to steal data and spread, turning a small event into a major loss.

metrics.name: Critical Vuln Patch Latency
metrics.question: How fast do we close the dangerous security holes attackers target first?
metrics.definition: The average number of days to deploy fixes for critical and high-severity vulnerabilities, measured from vendor disclosure or discovery to remediation.
metrics.boardFraming: Known, unpatched flaws are the most common way breaches happen; slow patching leaves an open door long after the risk is public.

metrics.name: Phishing Simulation Failure Rate
metrics.question: How likely are our employees to fall for a realistic phishing attack?
metrics.definition: The percentage of employees who clicked a link or entered credentials during simulated phishing exercises run in the reporting period.
metrics.boardFraming: Most breaches start with a single employee clicking a bad link; a high failure rate means our people are an open path into the business.

metrics.name: Security Training Completion
metrics.question: Have our people completed the training that helps them spot and avoid attacks?
metrics.definition: The percentage of in-scope employees who completed required security awareness training within the assigned period.
metrics.boardFraming: Untrained staff are easier targets; broad completion reduces the human mistakes behind most successful attacks.

metrics.name: MFA Coverage, Critical Systems
metrics.question: How well are our most sensitive accounts protected against stolen passwords?
metrics.definition: The percentage of critical systems and privileged accounts protected by multi-factor authentication rather than passwords alone.
metrics.boardFraming: Stolen passwords are cheap and common for attackers; multi-factor authentication is the single most effective, low-cost block against account takeover.

metrics.name: Open Critical Vulns Past SLA
metrics.question: How many serious security holes have we left open longer than our own deadline allows?
metrics.definition: The count of critical and high-severity vulnerabilities that remain unremediated beyond their internal service-level deadline at period end.
metrics.boardFraming: Each overdue flaw is a known risk we have chosen to leave open, and known-but-unfixed issues are a common finding after a breach.

metrics.name: High-Risk Vendors Unremediated
metrics.question: How many of our risky suppliers still have unresolved security problems?
metrics.definition: The count of high-risk third parties or vendors with identified security gaps that have not yet been remediated or accepted with a plan.
metrics.boardFraming: Attackers increasingly break in through weak suppliers; unresolved vendor risks extend our exposure to systems we do not fully control.

metrics.name: Overdue Compliance Findings
metrics.question: How many audit or compliance issues are past their deadline to fix?
metrics.definition: The count of internal or external audit and compliance findings that remain open past their agreed remediation due date.
metrics.boardFraming: Overdue findings signal control gaps that can trigger regulatory penalties, failed audits, and lost customer or partner trust.

metrics.name: Backup Restore Test Success
metrics.question: If we lost our data tomorrow, could we actually get it back?
metrics.definition: The percentage of scheduled backup restore tests that successfully recovered data within expected time and completeness during the period.
metrics.boardFraming: Backups only protect us if they actually restore; proven recovery is our last line of defense against ransomware and major outages.

metrics.name: Privileged Accounts Reviewed
metrics.question: Have we checked that only the right people still hold our most powerful access?
metrics.definition: The percentage of privileged and administrative accounts formally reviewed and re-certified for continued need during the reporting period.
metrics.boardFraming: Unchecked admin access (from role changes or departed staff) is a prime target for attackers and insiders; regular review shrinks that risk.
